resources.string:
This Privacy Policy explains how Project Lumen, an open-source eye-care and focus app (hereinafter "the app", "we", "us"), collects, uses, and protects information when you use the app on your device. Project Lumen is released under the Apache License 2.0. By installing or using the app you agree to the practices described in this policy. Effective date: August 7, 2026.
Project Lumen is designed to be local-first. The vast majority of your data never leaves your device. Unless you explicitly enable optional diagnostics or sign in with an email account, all statistics and settings remain on your device and are processed locally.
Local data. Eye-rest, focus, distance-to-screen, and ambient-light statistics are computed on your device and stored only in a local database on your device. This data is not uploaded to any server and is not shared with any third party.
Camera. The app uses the camera only for on-device distance-to-screen estimation and for blink and dry-eye analysis powered by ML Kit. Camera frames are analyzed in real time on your device; they are not saved, recorded, uploaded, or shared. You can revoke camera permission at any time through system settings; features that depend on the camera will stop working, while all other features remain available.
Optional diagnostics. Project Lumen includes optional diagnostics that are off by default: telemetry (usage statistics), crash reports, face-analysis samples, and an installed-app inventory. These are uploaded to the developer's backend only if you explicitly enable them. Each diagnostics category is independent and requires your explicit consent, which you grant or withdraw per category in the app settings. No diagnostics are sent until you opt in.
Telemetry consists of aggregated usage statistics used to improve the app. It contains no personally identifying information beyond the identifiers described in this policy.
Crash reports contain technical details about your device and the state of the app when an error occurred; they are used to diagnose and fix bugs.
If enabled, face-analysis samples may include anonymized analysis results used to improve distance and blink detection. They are uploaded only with your explicit consent.
The optional installed-app inventory lists the applications installed on your device and is used only to offer relevant focus or eye-care suggestions. It is uploaded only if you enable it.
Device installation ID. On first run the app generates a random installation identifier. It is stored in an encrypted credential store on your device and is used for device identity, integrity and attestation checks, and request signing. Reinstalling the app regenerates this identifier.
Optional cloud account. If you choose to sign in with an email address for cloud backup and synchronization, the account email and the synced backup are handled by the developer's backend.
Cloud backup may include your preferences and statistics. Backups are associated with your account and are used only to restore and synchronize your data across your own devices.
You can sign out at any time. You can also request deletion of your account and the associated backup data; the app provides a way to do this, and such requests are honored promptly.
Permissions. The app requests certain device permissions. Each permission is used only for the purpose stated on the App Permissions page.
Notifications and exact alarms. The app uses notifications and exact alarms to schedule eye-rest reminders and timers. The exact alarm permission allows the app to show reminders at the exact scheduled time.
Camera. Used for distance-to-screen measurement and blink and dry-eye detection as described above.
Display over other apps. The overlay permission allows the app to draw eye-care overlays over other apps. The overlay displays only eye-care content and does not intercept your private input unless you use features that explicitly require interaction.
Modify system settings. This permission is used to adjust screen brightness automatically when the auto-brightness feature is enabled.
Usage access. If you enable focus or usage tracking, usage access lets the app read which apps you use and for how long, in order to show focus statistics and reminders. This data is processed locally.
Boot. This permission allows the app to restore your scheduled reminders after your device restarts.
Full-screen intent and foreground services. These allow the app to show time-sensitive reminders and to keep eye-care monitoring running while the app is in the background.
Internet and network. Network access is used only to download optional resources, to communicate with the developer's backend when optional diagnostics or cloud sync are enabled, and to check the official repository for updates.
Your rights. You may access and correct data stored locally in the app, delete local data, export your local data, withdraw consent at any time, and stop using the service.
Withdrawal of consent. The app provides "withdraw consent" and "withdraw privacy policy consent" actions in Settings > About > App Declaration. Withdrawing consent stops the corresponding processing without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal.
Data retention. Local data is stored on your device until you delete it or uninstall the app. Clearing app data or uninstalling the app removes locally stored statistics.
Data uploaded through optional diagnostics is retained only as long as necessary for the purpose for which it was collected. You can stop the upload at any time by disabling the corresponding diagnostic category or by withdrawing consent.
We do not sell personal data and do not share it for monetary value. Project Lumen contains no third-party advertising SDKs. Analytics, when enabled, are disclosed and remain opt-in.
Children. The app is not directed at children under 13 years of age, or the minimum age of digital consent in your region. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children.
Changes to this policy. We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. When we do, we will revise the effective date at the top of this document and, where required, notify you within the app. Continued use of the app after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
Contact. This app is open source. The latest version of this Privacy Policy and the contact and issue channels are available in the official GitHub repository.
